current_answer: Current evidence supports seven distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a public group proposal-and-vote route for the next scene; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end VSA queue-and-playout route; FastVideo FastH3 Preview has local clip paths; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining an unattended dense FastH3 channel at 22.1 fps through 448×448 output, prequeued prompts, and retimed playout; Comfy’s optimized H3 path broadens local access; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate OpenAI-compatible H3 service for T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA. The latter is a deployment route, not a live-video result: its published four-B300, 50-step FL2VA row takes 86.964 seconds to return about 8.71 seconds of 24-fps output.

catalogue_card.question: Does an OpenAI H3 endpoint make AI video live?
catalogue_card.text: vLLM-Omni documents a remote H3 service, but its stated four-B300 full-H3 baseline returns about 8.7 seconds of video in about 87 seconds. Useful API route; no live-video proof.

summary: vLLM-Omni documents an OpenAI-compatible H3 service for T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA that a remote ComfyUI client can call.

Its stated full-H3 four-B300 FL2VA row returns 209 frames at 1248×768 in 86.964 seconds mean HTTP client latency. At 24 fps, that is about 8.71 seconds of output: roughly ten seconds of work per output second.
The published row is a named, warmed full-H3 workload. It does not establish a FastH3/Turbo result, quality, cost, queue capacity, client-to-visible latency, continuous delivery, or interaction.

Yoroll’s collective next-scene route, fal’s held Director session, Reactor’s buffered FastH3 route, the one-5090 FastH3 channel, and local ComfyUI H3 remain distinct routes with different control, deployment, continuity, and hardware contracts.
uncertainty: vLLM-Omni’s H3 serving and four-B300 result are maintainer documentation for one warmed full-H3 FL2VA workload; the pool has not operated it or measured cost, quality, queueing, failure behavior, or client-to-visible latency.
Yoroll’s YoLive control loop and H3 Superfast timing are company launch claims; the pool did not observe a live vote, measure end-to-end response, or independently reproduce the eight-B200 result.
The one-RTX-5090 FastH3 channel is a community project’s one-machine self-report; the pool has not run or independently audited it, and its downloadable files are access-gated.
Reactor’s playout, continuity, and four- or eight-B200 timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
freshness_note: Checked 17 September 2026. vLLM-Omni’s remote H3 route is newly documented, with one named four-B300 full-H3 latency baseline. It expands deployment options; it does not establish a live, continuous, interactive, or costed service.
